title: Dynamic enterprise export intake orchestration and SLA-driven prioritization
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Enterprise customers submit ad-hoc console/reporting requests (large CSV/Parquet exports, cost breakdown joins, tenant-level consumption bundles) via support, CSMs, and the Console. Current intake is manual, inconsistent, and leads to missed SLAs, untracked engineering effort, and repeated back-and-forth for schema and residency constraints.

Goal: Build an opinionated intake orchestration layer for enterprise reporting requests that: 1) provides consistent metadata capture (schema, estimated row count, retention/residency, PII flags, query complexity), 2) applies an automated priority/sla score, and 3) surfaces clear fulfillment lanes (self-serve, ops-assisted, engineering-required) with estimated delivery windows. The system should produce a machine-readable request record that drives routing to Console exports, Ad-hoc ETL jobs, or Dedicated/Private data connectors.

Scope: MVP focuses on non-bug requests for usage analytics, tenant cost breakdown exports, and dashboard data extracts initiated by enterprise customers or CSMs. We will not build the export execution engine in this ticket — this is intake, scoring, and routing only.

Out-of-scope: realtime streaming integrations, automated content transformation, or full export executions for very large archival jobs (these will be handled by engineering runbooks and Dedicated ops lanes).
acceptance_criteria: A web form and API endpoint exist to capture request metadata: purpose, schema fields, expected rows, data residency, PII indicator, requester and workspace, urgency
An automated scoring function runs on submission and assigns SLA category (48h / 5d / 2w) and fulfillment lane (self-serve / ops-assisted / eng-required)
Console UI shows a queue with sortable columns for SLA, score, workspace tier, and estimated effort, visible to PM/Ops/CSM
Requests tagged with 'eng-required' create a linked ENG ticket stub with captured metadata and a suggested estimate
Audit trail stored as a request record with links to customer conversation, Confluence spec, or GH PR (if applicable)
Telemetry emitted for intake volume, average scoring distribution, and % auto-routed to self-serve
Security gating: any request with PII flag requires explicit Security review flag and blocks automatic routing until cleared
decisions: Use a lightweight JSON schema for request payloads to allow machine-readable handoff to eng/ops
Adopt a rules + points based scoring model (factors: row-estimate, join complexity, PII, residency, tier SLA, historical rework)
Default to conservative SLAs for first 30 days, then tighten thresholds based on telemetry
Integrate with existing Console Request Queue and CSM workspace view (no new landing page in MVP)

notes: Rationale: Standardizing intake reduces time lost to clarification loops, creates clean handoffs for engineering, and enables measurable SLAs for enterprise customers.
Risk: Over-automation may mis-route complex exports. Mitigation: keep a low bar for escalation and require human review on 'eng-required' lane.
Fallback: If scoring proves brittle in pilot, fall back to CSM triage with mandatory eng-approval for high cost jobs.
